After paying full price for the Deluxe Edition and playing the game for two weeks I fully believe this should have just been a new DLC for Sniper Elite 5. If you are a die hard fan you will enjoy some new maps but there aren't enough to justify the price. The maps feel less interactive compared to SE5 i.e. not being able to many scale walls and ledges or hop over barriers like you would expect to. It also feels like less thought was put into the gameplay, level design, and the placement of enemies. Heavily recycled game assets from SE5 contribute to my argument that it is simply an expansion pack. Comes off as more of a cash grab than an evolution of the Franchise. Resistance definitely did not meet my expectations for one of my favorite game franchises. I hope Rebellion listens to the overwhelming negative feedback and makes improvements.

I kind of grabbed this just to 100% the game (which took about 47hrs) and I ended up really enjoying the grind for it.

The campaign, having played SE4 and still yet to play SE5, felt pretty standard; solid and enjoyable. Visually the game looks good, not much to say there. The little side missions after collecting posters was surprisingly fun as well though even on authentic they felt a little easy to 3 star. Survival mode was cool but that was just a means to grinding the guns out fast for me, probably better co-op though.

Now the meat for me was really invasion mode. Having invaders come into my campaign and completely change the course of how my mission was going was really nice. I'm the type of player to hardcore stealth with traps/decoys, which can play really well in your favor, the panic in those first few invasions really can force you to take the loud route if you panic and it just adds layers to the mental game against another player. Camping is kind of possible which is annoying a bit but in my time I've yet to lose to someone hard camping. There's a lot of things they could do with invasion but I ask they start with maybe a text chat or proximity voice chat maybe even death comms would be very fun.

I'll end with a 4/5. The multiplayer connection at times being tied to one person and ending the game was irritating for how long some matches can be (not to be confused with campaign co-op/invasion that worked fine). These maps were not really my cup of tea, and the one I actually liked is DLC.

Well, it took them 3 years to get this game out, which was a bit of a stretch of time, but I think it was worth it. I have some gripes of my own about the game, but I still enjoy playing it. First off is the engine of the game. It's basically SE5, with a new protagonist (who voice must have been done by Jason Statham, because he sounds just like him, IMO. What is heard can't be unheard now). Everyone is complaining about the price? WHY? At $49.99 and with 8 missions, or rather 6.5, that comes out to around 8 bucks a mission, give or take a few cents. That's not considering the PVP maps and the propaganda missions. That's not bad considering some of the past SE5 DLC's were one map and they cost 10 bucks. Some of the maps are reminiscent of past maps in my opinion, i.e. Lock, Stock, and Barrels map has a touch of the SE5's Occupied Residence in it). There is one particular item that I miss from SE4 that they took out of SE5 and wasn't included in this one as well, and that's the Trip Mine. I just don't see the appeal of the Shu Mine.  Anyway, I'm enjoying the game and hope they pump out more of them.

I really enjoyed this installment of the series, and would definitely recommend it to others that like the Sniper Elite game loop. 

Pros: The maps are well designed. I've read the criticism that the maps seem a bit sparse, but I find having less mobs running around, allows me to play in a more thoughtful sniper-like way. I really take a lot of time on each map - sometimes spending 3+hrs to complete each mission. In previous incarnations of the game, you could have maps with so many mobs that stealth was nearly impossible for large portions of the map.

Cons: My biggest gripe with SI:R is the occasional glitches controlling my character. For instance, there is one map with an observation post, and taking the ladder to the top simply knocks you to the ground (giving you fall damage) instead of allowing you in the observation post. Other times, my characters animation would get stuck when I would try to come out of a hiding to melee an enemy. Despite these Cons being annoying, they were rare enough that it did not distract from my enjoyment of the game.

A couple of suggestions to the developers - It would be nice to have the enemy AI be incrementally more aware of thier surroundings.. Mobs should not talk or have animations designed to let fellow enemies know they are in trouble if no other enemies are in sight.

I would also like the sound of the bullet when it goes into the kill cam to match the weapon you are shooting, and not the same generic gun shot sound.
